title: Road paving contract and veterans' crosswalks approved
subtitle: Also: tree canopy grant, fee study consultant, development charge deferrals, Belwood post office lease, data centre notice of motion.
overview: Council awarded the 2026 road asphalting contract to Cox Construction Limited at $2,768,878.98 including contingency and excluding HST {{vote:m8}}. It also approved a $250,000 single-source contract for a road base stabilization bio-resin on Sixth Line East, and directed staff to negotiate added work on two sections within the approved budget, subject to Ministerial approval.

Council approved decorative veterans' crosswalks at the Elora and Fergus cenotaphs, funded from the General Capital Reserve {{vote:m10}}. It accepted a federal grant agreement for an urban forest inventory {{vote:m7}} and chose a consultant for a Community Services fee study with a $75,000 upset limit {{vote:m9}}.

Ahead of the municipal election, council delegated authority to the Chief Administrative Officer to sign development charge deferral agreements until October 1, 2026 {{vote:m11}}, and to arrange a lease for the Belwood post office space {{vote:m12}}. A Councillor's notice of motion on data centres was added to the agenda and is to be listed for the August 24 meeting. After a closed session, the minutes record no public announcement.

decisions.detail: Council awarded Request for Tender #48-26 to Cox Construction Limited, approved a $250,000 single-source bio-resin contract for Sixth Line East, and directed staff to negotiate expanded scope for Sections 2 and 13.
Staff will install non-standard decorative crosswalks at the Elora and Fergus cenotaphs, with the estimated $40,000 excluding HST funded from the General Capital Reserve.
Staff may negotiate and award the study to Watson & Associates Economists Ltd. to an upset limit of $75,000, with funding revised as set out in the report.
The Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer may sign the Federation of Canadian Municipalities grant agreement for the urban forest resilience and natural asset management initiative.
The Chief Administrative Officer may execute development charge deferral agreements consistent with By-law 2026-23 between July 30 and October 1, 2026.
The Chief Administrative Officer may enter into a lease of part of 8460 Wellington Road 19 for a post office, subject to the Township's solicitor's review.

debate: On the fee study, councillors asked why only one proposal came back from an invitational process and whether an open call might attract more bidders. Staff said they could not predict the outcome of an open call, which would delay the study. They expected extra funding would be needed either way because the scope had grown.

One councillor asked whether the cost could be capped nearer $50,000. Staff said the broader scope and enhanced engagement with affected groups justified the $75,000 limit. Another councillor urged that all event-hosting groups be consulted, not just one or two.

Councillors asked about equity-deserving groups and charitable organizations. Staff said the study will assess possible fee subsidies for those groups, covering all fees, and that council will later decide how much to subsidize.

On road work, councillors asked about the Jefferson Elora Community Centre parking lot, Bridge Street and Tower Street, line painting and Fergus Curling Club timing. Staff said the parking lot is expected to be a 2027 budget request and that work timing will be set after award.

On the crosswalks, staff moved the Fergus location to the Norman Craig Square entrances because of traffic volumes. They said paint should cost less than the estimate, and both legions could not commit to long-term maintenance but were open to an annual contribution.
